A relay checks that it is you, and nothing else. Once paired, this device can run commands on that computer, exactly as a terminal on it could. Pair a relay On the computer running the harness, open /relay/pair. It shows a QR code and an eight-digit code; either one works, and both expire after a few minutes. Scan QR code Point the camera at the code on the relay\'s pairing page Or type the code Relay address https://192.168.1.5:3443 Pairing code Name for this device Pair Pairing… The scanned code carries this relay\'s key, so it is checked before anything is sent. A typed address carries no key, so this trusts whatever answers the first time. Scanning the QR code checks it instead. This address is not encrypted, so the token and everything you send travel in the clear. That is not a relay pairing code. That code comes from a newer relay (version %1$d) than this app understands. Update 神言神语. That code has expired. Reload the relay\'s pairing page for a new one. The relay refused that code. Codes work once and expire after a few minutes — reload the pairing page and try the new one. Too many attempts. Wait %1$d seconds and try again. %1$s answered, but it does not accept pairing. Use the address the relay printed when it started, not the harness\'s own. Could not reach %1$s. Check the address, and that the relay is running and reachable from this phone. The key at %1$s is not the one this code names. Do not pair — something else may be answering at that address. Enter the relay address, including https:// Enter the code shown on the relay\'s pairing page. %1$s is a relay, but it refuses requests addressed this way — the code was never read. Add that address to publicHostnames in the relay\'s cordis.patch.yml and restart, or reach the relay by an address it already knows. Attach file Remove file Uploading… Upload failed. Tap to retry.
